w: Swamishri’s fever and cough had persisted all night long. In the morning, after completing his puja, Swamishri wished to go for Thakorji’s darshan. The doctor and Swamishri’s attendant sadhus explained that it was cold outside and with the fever and cold it would be better if he did not go. But Swamishri insisted and went for darshan.
After breakfast Swamishri retired for rest.
In the evening, while having dinner Swamishri was extremely pleased on hearing the report of the recent Kishore Shibir in London.

In the morning, Swamishri performed the murti-pratishtha of Akshar Purushottam Maharaj and Guru parampara at Karakhadi. Swamishri left Karakhadi and arrived in Tithor at 6.25 pm and performed the murti-pratishtha of Akshar Purushottam Maharaj (canvas murtis) and Guru parampara. Thereafter, Swamishri blessed a large assembly.
Swamishri sanctified the land for the new proposed mandirs in Rajbodeli and Kashipura.
In the evening, Swamishri went to Kosindra and blessed an assembly. Then the devotees honored Lord Harikrishna Maharaj.
One hundred and thirty five couples were engaged in the yagna rituals and 12 Brahmin children were given the sacred thread by Swamishri. Thereafter, Swamishri performed the pujan of the murtis.

In the evening at 6.00 pm, Swamishri arrived at the boat station called Meadow Bank on the river Paramatta to embark upon a procession (nagar yatra) by boat. Two boats had been hired for the ritual procession of the murtis. In the first boat, 'Royal Boat', the murtis of Akshar Purushottam Maharaj, Radha Krishna Dev, Shiv Parvatiji, Ganpatiji, Sita Ram and Hanumanji were installed on its upper deck. Swamishri and 250 devotees sailed in the 'Royal Boat'. About 600 devotees were in the second boat called 'Lady Wakehurst'. The procession on the river (sagar yatra) commenced at 6.10 pm. The sadhus sang the Swaminarayan dhun and bhajans all through the procession. The boat passed beneath the famous Sydney Harbour Bridge and the Opera House. Thereafter, arti was performed and prayer-verses were sung. Then, Swamishri bathed Shri Harikrishna Maharaj with the local river water and sprinkled it on everyone. A small potful of the sanctified water was emptied into the river water and Swamishri wished for the liberation of all living things in it. The boat-procession concluded at 7.45 pm.

As a prelude to the murti-pratishtha rituals of the murtis of Shri Ghanshyam Maharaj, Shri Nilkanth Varni and Guru Parampara a yagna was held. There were 101 Brahmins chanting the yagna mantras in the presence of 1,437 participants (yajmans). Shrutiprakash Swami and Bhadresh Swami were coordinating and conducting the rituals. Besides the murtis mentioned the murtis of Shri Akshar Purushottam Maharaj (Hiravadi, Amdavad), and Shri Akshar Purushottam Maharaj, Shri Harikrishna Maharaj, Shri Lakshmi-Narayan Dev, Shri Hanumanji and Shri Ganapatiji (Bamangam) and the canvas murtis for Pipliya village were placed in the yagna hall. Swamishri and the senior sadhus performed the yagna rituals. Thereafter Swamishri performed pujan and arti of all the murtis and the kalashes. Finally in his blessings Swamishri said, “The pratishtha ritual of Shri Ghanshyam Maharaj is being held on the day of Shastriji Maharaj’s birthday anniversary. When God is invoked, he resides (in the murti) with his divine power and glory. It is then that we derive happiness (from the murti). That is why the yagna rituals are performed. This yagna is being performed for peace. And when the murti of God is consecrated there is peace. Then bhakti blossoms in our heart. And when his moral commands and upasana are followed then one experiences inner peace” Thereafter Swamishri presided over the birthday celebration assembly of Shastriji Maharaj. After a traditional dance performance by youths Mahant Swami addressed the assembly. Finally, Swamishri blessed the gathering, “Shastriji Maharaj came on earth to give happiness to all; the happiness of God and the joy of bhajan85 One has taken infinite births – as a king, Indra, etc. – and then one has got this human birth. In the former births one has gratified the senses with worldly pleasures but one has not attained peace and moksha. Without moksha there is no peace. Even if you were to eat the best of foods now, in the evening you will be hungry again. So, material happiness is fleeting. However when one becomes atmarup or brahmarup there is no need for eating, drinking, seeing and moving. In the happiness of God lies all happiness. In view of Akshar’s vision we are all in Akshardham. If one realizes this then one will not be inclined to return home from here” At 3.15 pm a grand procession of the murtis was carried out in the city of Vadodara. The procession commenced from the grounds of Navlakhi then proceeded towards Kirtisthambh, Market, Lal Court, Gandhinagar Gruh, Amdavadi Pol, Ravpura (tower), Kothi and finally terminated at the Navlakhi ground. All the senior sadhus, 200 sadhus, 4,200 male devotees and 5,700 female devotees, 10,000 in all, participated in the grand procession. The 1.5 km colourful pageant included youths on horseback, a music band, and troupes of dancing children and tribal devotees. Women carried the auspicious pots on their head while singing bhajans. The procession concluded at 6.00 pm.
ph: Murti-pratishtha pujan of Brahmaswarup Shastriji Maharaj
Swamishri performs murti-pratishtha pujan of Shri Hanumanji and Shri Ganapatiji

w: A family wrote to Swamishri: "Gold jewellery that we put away with our own hands has gone missing from our home. This has happened twice, and money also goes missing like this. We have a ghar mandir at home and sadhus have visited, so why does this happen? We cannot understand. Could some ancestor be troubling us?"

Reading the letter, Swamishri said, "You have a mandir at home and the sadhus have visited, so there is no need now for any superstition that ancestors are troubling you. Still, so that the doubt leaves your mind, recite God's Janmangal Namavali five times every day. God will make everything right."

And Swamishri's words proved true. With the Janmangal Namavali the superstition went away, and instead of blaming ancestors they watched more carefully, and within a few days the secret came out. It became clear that it was not the ancestors but a servant in the house.

Today during Swamishri's meal the jholi festival came up. Viveksagar Swami said, "I often say in my talks that Shastriji Maharaj built mandirs by begging with a jholi, and the last witness of that jholi is Pramukh Swami Maharaj alone. Everyone else asks with the jholi now, but compared with the situation and need of that time, today's jholi is asking just for the sake of asking."

Swamishri said, "We had to go begging every 15 days, and we would get handfuls of dal and rice." Saying this, he laughed and said to Gunsagar Swami sitting in front, "You get to tour America, London, everywhere."
Gunsagar Swami said, "That is all by your grace! Even now, whatever comes, comes in your name. Otherwise who would ask about us? We ask for donations in your name and people give."

Swamishri said, "Whether we ask or you ask, whether here or there, it is God who gives everything. It is the glory of Shastriji Maharaj and Yogiji Maharaj, so it comes in their name. Would anything come in our name?" Swamishri placed all the credit at the feet of his gurus.
Viveksagar Swami said, "If we talk of Delhi Akshardham, that happened only by your glory."

Swamishri said, "Delhi seems a miracle. I cannot understand how Akshardham came about! The devotees' donations came by themselves, the materials came, the stone came out of the quarry and a chain formed. It got carved, it got filled, and when it arrived there the fitting got done. I never knew how it happened!" Swamishri spoke in wonder, as if he knew nothing of it.
A sadhu said, "But you were the one who brought the donations."

Swamishri said, "Not me. It was Shastriji Maharaj and Yogiji Maharaj. Their glory. Yogi Bapa's resolve was so strong that money came by itself. The work too fell into place so that everything happened by itself, and that it happened in a short time was also their glory."

Viveksagar Swami said, "You say the work fell into place, but if you were not at the root, how would it fall into place? This is like Deva Bhagat. Once Deva Bhagat came with a plan and said, 'One wheel turns a second, the second turns a third, the third turns a fourth, and in this way electricity is made.' Then I said, 'That is fine, the fourth turns the third and the third turns the second, but what turns the first wheel? How does it turn?' And Deva Bhagat said, 'Oh, it just turns.' In the same way you say the stones came by themselves and everything fell into place, but if you were not there, how would the other wheels have turned?"
Swamishri said, "It is all the glory of Shastriji Maharaj and Yogiji Maharaj."
Swamishri would not take the credit for such a grand work upon himself, and he did not. He placed it at his gurus' feet, quite naturally.
